references.text: This text confirms the same relationship where the Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand, which is the basis for the Son to show and do the Father's works.
Here the principle is elaborated that the Son can do nothing of himself, but only what he sees the Father doing, as directly explained in verse 20 where the Father shows him everything.
Jesus' statement that he always does what is pleasing to the Father and that the Father is with him emphasizes the same unity in action and showing mentioned in verse 20.
Jesus' argument that if he does not do the Father's works, they should not believe in him points directly to the fact that the Father's works are those shown and done by the Son.
Here it is confirmed that the Father who dwells in the Son does his own works, which is the same dynamic where the Father shows and does works through the Son.

Jesus' distinction between servant and friend is based on the fact that he has made known to the disciples everything he heard from the Father, reflecting how the Father shows everything he does to the Son.
Jesus' prayer that the disciples may see his glory, which the Father has given him, connects to the Father showing greater works so that people will marvel.
